subject: Numeric literals
notes: "A literal shall contain at least one digit." (cite.py --check 8.3.3.3.2 -> OK §8.3.3.3.2 1)). Enforced by construction in the lexer: INT_BODY is [0-9]+, DEC_BODY is [0-9]+ '.' [0-9]+ | '.' [0-9]+, SIGNED_*LIT are [+-] followed by those bodies, and numericLiteralCore's comma alternatives (INTEGERLIT COMMA INTEGERLIT | COMMA INTEGERLIT) each carry an INTEGERLIT. No token or parser alternative forms a numeric literal from a bare sign or a bare decimal point, so a digitless 'literal' can only be a parse error. Structural rule; no probe needed beyond confirming the fragments. No dedicated negative golden -> test-ref empty. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the formation/value rules are unchanged across editions; only the digit ceiling moves: 18 at COBOL-85, 1 through 31 from 2002 per the clause's lead paragraph)]
